newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to send officials for China shipping talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to send officials for China shipping talks.

text.p: Taiwan has agreed to send transport officials to take part in talks on direct shipping links between the island and the mainland, a senior government official said on Monday.

Hsieh Ming-hui, department head of navigation and aviation under the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, and another transport official would join the discussion, said Kao Koong-lian, vice chairman of the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council.

Taiwan said the officials would attend the meeting on Wednesday in Hong Kong, sponsored by shipping executives from Taiwan and China, in their private capacities and would only assist local executives in resolving technical problems.
"The meeting will discuss the operations of (Taiwan's) offshore transshipment centre, it will only involve technical aspects," Kao said on state television.
Kao said the officials would not be involved in sensitive political dialogue with their mainland counterparts.
The two sides were expected to discuss the inaugural direct shipping links between Taiwan's southern port of Kaohsiung and China's southeastern Xiamen and Fuzhou during the meeting.

To fulfil its ambition of becoming an Asia-Pacific business hub, Taiwan proposed in 1995 to set up an offshore transshipment centre at Kaohsiung, from which ships would be allowed to sail directly between Taiwan and China.
The project has been delayed by sovereignty issues.

Last August China unveiled rules governing direct shipping links across the Taiwan strait, effective immediately, but Taiwan gave a cool response, saying Beijing's rules were "mingled with sensitive political issues".
Taiwan has banned direct air and shipping links with China since Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists lost the civil war to the Chinese communists and fled to the island in 1949.

With tensions easing since the late 1980s, civilian aircraft and vessels have skirted the ban by stopping over in a third country or territory such as the British colony of Hong Kong or Portuguese-run Macau.
Taiwanese businessmen, who have poured more than $20 billion into China, have exerted pressure on the government to establish such links to save transportation costs.
